lines.text: A box showed up on my porch. It's full of things I haven't lost *yet.*
A cardboard box. Old tape. A label in thick black marker. *Lost and Found.* And my name.
On top, my house keys. But my keys are in my pocket. Same scratches. Same dumb bottle-opener keychain.
My wallet. My headphones. My phone, with a cracked screen. *My* phone isn't cracked.
The next morning, I dropped my phone. It cracked. *The exact same crack.*
So the box isn't giving things back. It's *early.*
I dug deeper. My watch. My glasses. My dog's collar. Her tag still jingles. She's asleep on the couch.
Every day, something from the box goes missing for real. The keys on Tuesday. The headphones on Wednesday.
And every night, something *new* shows up in the box.
At the very bottom, there's a smaller box. Taped shut. With its own label.
It just says my name. And *tomorrow's date.*
Taped inside the lid of the big box, there's a note. In *my* handwriting.
